topic: Task-Based versus Thread-Based for Result and Exception Propagation
explanation: Assumption: If a function throws an exception while running asynchronously, it can be caught by the caller regardless of the execution mechanism. Reality: When using the thread-based approach (`std::thread`), an unhandled exception thrown in the asynchronously executed function causes the entire program to terminate via `std::terminate`. Why It Fails: The thread-based approach provides no mechanism for communicating exceptions back to the parent scope. In contrast, the task-based approach (`std::async`) returns an `std::future`, and the `get()` function on that future is designed to capture and re-throw any exceptions, allowing the caller to handle them safely, alongside retrieving return values.
practical_example: A developer runs a computationally intensive validation task using `std::thread`. If the validation hits bad input and throws, the entire web server process terminates unexpectedly, whereas using `std::async` would isolate the failure and allow the server to return an error code.
keywords: std::thread exception propagation, Task-based exception handling, std::terminate thread exception, asynchronous exception handling
chapter: Item 35: Prefer task-based programming to thread-based programming.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
